texts.li: [their:tribal|their:medieval] {GIVER}, a factor of {FACTION} from {PLACE}, has more goods than the caravan's pack animals can carry. {GIVER} asks the colony to keep {COUNT} sealed crates until the end of the season.
[their:industrial] {GIVER}, a factor of {FACTION} from {PLACE}, has more goods than the trucks can carry this trip. {GIVER} asks the colony to keep {COUNT} sealed crates until the end of the season.
[their:spacer] {GIVER}, a factor of {FACTION} from {PLACE}, has more cargo than the next shuttle can lift. {GIVER} asks the colony to keep {COUNT} sealed crates until the end of the season.

li.label: Accept
li.outcome: The factor will bring the crates.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: The factor will find somewhere else to keep the crates.

lines.li: [kept] All here and dry, thank you.
[lost] Some of these crates are not as we left them.
[thanks] Everything is here, and here is your pay for the keeping.
[cold] I'll take what is left of my goods.

terms.li: [their:tribal|their:medieval] {GIVER} brings the crates within a day of the colony agreeing, and porters set them down by the stores. Keep them under a roof, and do not open, sell or lose any of them. After {DAYS}, a clerk of {FACTION} comes to count them.\n\nIf all of them are there, sealed and dry, {GIVER} will come for them later in the season and pay {SILVER} silver for the keeping. A crate left out in the rain or snow for half a day is spoiled. For any crate lost, opened, sold or spoiled, {GIVER} will ask the colony to pay what it was worth.

[their:industrial] {GIVER} brings the crates within a day of the colony agreeing, and porters set them down by the stores. Keep them under a roof, and do not open, sell or lose any of them. After {DAYS}, a clerk of {FACTION} comes to count them.\n\nIf all of them are there, sealed and dry, {GIVER} will come for them later in the season and pay {SILVER} silver for the keeping. A crate left out in the rain or snow for half a day is spoiled. For any crate lost, opened, sold or spoiled, {GIVER} will ask the colony to pay what it was worth.

[their:spacer] {GIVER}'s shuttle drops the crates by the stores within a day of the colony agreeing. Keep them under a roof, and do not open, sell or lose any of them. After {DAYS}, a clerk of {FACTION} comes to count them.\n\nIf all of them are there, sealed and dry, {GIVER} will come for them later in the season and pay {SILVER} silver for the keeping. A crate left out in the rain or snow for half a day is spoiled. For any crate lost, opened, sold or spoiled, {GIVER} will ask the colony to pay what it was worth.

accepted.li: {GIVER} of {FACTION} is on the way with {COUNT} crates. Keep them under a roof and sealed for {DAYS}.

reminder.li: A clerk of {FACTION} comes to count {GIVER}'s crates within {DAYS}.

notes.li: [wet] Rain or snow is falling on one of {GIVER}'s crates. Move it under a roof, or the goods inside will spoil.
[spoiled] One of {GIVER}'s crates stood in the rain or snow too long, and the goods inside are spoiled.
[clerk] A clerk of {FACTION} has come to count {GIVER}'s crates.

ends.li: [kept] The clerk of {FACTION} counted all {COUNT} of {GIVER}'s crates. They are sealed and dry.\n\n{GIVER} will come for them later in the season and pay {SILVER} silver for the keeping.
[lost] The clerk of {FACTION} counted {GIVER}'s crates. {ITEM} of the {COUNT} are missing, opened, sold or spoiled.\n\n{GIVER} will send word about what the colony owes for them.

texts.li: [!samepeople] A few days ago the clerk of {FACTION} found all of {GIVER}'s crates safe and dry. Now {RIVAL}, a trader of {OTHERPEOPLE}, wants to meet the colony at the gate. {RIVAL} wants to buy the crates without {GIVER} knowing.

[samepeople] A few days ago the clerk of {FACTION} found all of {GIVER}'s crates safe and dry. Now {RIVAL}, another trader of {FACTION}, wants to meet the colony at the gate. {RIVAL} wants to buy the crates without {GIVER} knowing.

li.label: Agree to meet
li.outcome: The trader is on the way.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: The colony will not meet the trader.

lines.li: [offer] I'll pay well for those crates, and nobody needs to know.
[sold] Good, my people will be glad of these.
[refused] That's a pity, it was a good price.
[told] You told the factor, so we have nothing more to talk about.

terms.li: If the colony agrees, {RIVAL} comes to the gate within a day and offers {SILVER} silver for all the crates. The colony can sell them, refuse, or refuse and send word to {GIVER}.\n\nIf the colony sells, {GIVER} may find out who bought them and ask the colony to pay for them. If the colony does not meet {RIVAL}, nothing changes, and {GIVER} comes for the crates later in the season.

accepted.li: {RIVAL} of {OTHERPEOPLE} is on the way to the colony's gate.

ends.li: [sold] {RIVAL} paid {SILVER} silver for {GIVER}'s crates, and the colony's people are taking them out to {RIVAL} at the gate. {GIVER} will come for the crates later in the season.
[refused] The colony refused {RIVAL}'s offer, and {RIVAL} left without the crates. {GIVER} will come for them later in the season.
[told] The colony refused {RIVAL}'s offer and sent word to {GIVER} about it. {FACTION} think better of the colony for it. {GIVER} will come for the crates later in the season.

texts.li: {RIVAL} of {OTHERPEOPLE} is at the gate and offers {SILVER} silver for {GIVER}'s {COUNT} crates, which is well over what they are worth. {RIVAL} says {GIVER} never needs to know who bought them.\n\nIf the colony sells, it is paid now, and the crates are carried out to {RIVAL}. {GIVER} comes for the crates later in the season and will find them gone.

li.label: Sell the crates
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} paid, and the crates are being carried out to {X_objective}.

li.label: Refuse, and tell the factor
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} left without the crates, and the colony sent word to the factor.

texts.li: When the clerk of {FACTION} counted {GIVER}'s crates, {COUNT} were missing, opened, sold or spoiled. {GIVER} asks the colony to pay what they were worth.

li.label: Agree to pay
li.outcome: The colony will put the silver aside.

li.label: Refuse
li.outcome: The factor's people will come for the crates that are left.

terms.li: {GIVER} asks for {SILVER} silver within {DAYS}. Once the silver is in the colony's stockpiles, {GIVER}'s people come for it.\n\nIf the colony pays, {GIVER}'s people take the rest of the crates and the matter is settled. If it does not pay in time, {FACTION} will send no traders to the colony for a year.

accepted.li: The colony has {DAYS} to put {SILVER} silver in its stockpiles for {GIVER}.

reminder.li: {GIVER} expects {SILVER} silver in the colony's stockpiles within {DAYS}.

notes.li: [ready] The silver for {GIVER} is in the stockpiles. People of {FACTION} come for it within {DAYS}.

ends.li: [paid] People of {FACTION} have come for the {SILVER} silver. {GIVER}'s people will take the crates that are left, and the matter is settled.

titles.li: Pay the factor for the crates

texts.li: Some days ago the colony sold {GIVER}'s crates to {RIVAL}. {GIVER} has heard about the sale from traders on the road, and asks the colony to pay for them.

li.label: Agree to pay
li.outcome: The colony will put the silver aside.

lines.li: [guards] We are here with the factor's word: no more trade with you for a year.

terms.li: {GIVER} of {FACTION} asks for {SILVER} silver, what the crates were worth, within {DAYS}. Once the silver is in the colony's stockpiles, {GIVER}'s people come for it.\n\nIf the colony pays, the matter is settled, though {FACTION} will trust the colony less. If it does not pay, guards of {FACTION} will come to the gate, and {FACTION} will not trade with the colony for a year.

accepted.li: The colony has {DAYS} to put {SILVER} silver in its stockpiles for {GIVER}.

reminder.li: {GIVER} expects {SILVER} silver in the colony's stockpiles within {DAYS}.

notes.li: [ready] The silver for {GIVER} is in the stockpiles. People of {FACTION} come for it within {DAYS}.

ends.li: [paid] People of {FACTION} have come for the {SILVER} silver. The matter of the crates is settled, but {FACTION} trust the colony less.
